theorem_title: Shao's Lemma 2.3: the finite check at $m = 15$
natural_language_statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be sets of units modulo 15. If

$$|A||B| + |B||C| + |C||A| > 5(|A| + |B| + |C|)$$

then every residue $x$ modulo 15 can be written $x = a + b + c$ with $a \in A$, $b \in B$ and $c \in C$.

There are eight units modulo 15, so the hypothesis is a finite condition on three integers in $[0,8]$. Thirty-four unordered size triples satisfy it, of which $(2,7,8)$, $(3,6,7)$, $(4,5,7)$, $(4,6,6)$ and $(5,5,6)$ are the minimal ones under componentwise order.
source: Xuancheng Shao, "A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem", Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, arXiv:1206.6139v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139, Lemma 2.3
